the following questions: Given a set of points in the plane, what is the best way to refine a triangulation so that the resulting triangles satisfy certain quality criteria? How can we compute a triangulation with the best possible quality? What is the complexity of the best possible algorithm?

the new algorithm is a significant improvement over the Ruppert's algorithm.
the Delaunay triangulation is the best known data structure for the mesh generation problem.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our algorithm is the first to achieve the best of both worlds.
we have shown that Delaunay triangulations can be refined in sub-quadratic time, and that Delaunary refinement is competitive with quadtree methods.
we have a refinement algorithm with a subquadratic time complexity and comparable time bounds to quadtree methods.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Delaunay refinements are not inherently slower than quadtree methods.
the time bounds of Ruppert’s algorithm can be improved by using a simple and efficient technique for maintaining the Delaunay triangulation.
the time complexity of the refinement algorithm is not a major bottleneck for meshing algorithms.
